 PB1.1 - 8 Arnold Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
 Consideration Type: ACTION
 Ward: 5 - York South - Weston
 Origin
 (October 28, 2026) Report from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning
 Recommendations
 The Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning recommends that:
1. City Council state its intention to designate the property at 8 Arnold Avenue under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act in accordance with the Statement of Significance for 8 Arnold Avenue (Reasons for Designation) attached as Attachment 1, to the report, October 28, 2026, from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning.
2. If there are no objections to the designation, City Council authorize the City Solicitor to introduce the Bill in Council designating the property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act.
 Summary
 This report recommends that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 8 Arnold Avenue under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value according to the Statement of Significance and description of heritage attributes found in Attachment 1.
The subject property at 8 Arnold Avenue is located just within the northern boundary of the Rockcliffe-Smythe neighbourhood, south of Lambton Avenue. The residence is notable as a red-brick, one-and-a-half-storey, Ontario Farmhouse-style property, dating from c.1870s – 1880s, and historically known as the George Marshall Residence. The property, which is the earliest known house in the Mount Dennis community, serves to recall the community’s former farming and settlement past. A location map and current photograph of the property are found in Attachment 2.
In 2021 the Mount Dennis Cultural Heritage Resource Assessment (CHRA) was completed by the heritage consulting firm, Common Bond Collective, as part of the Picture Mount Dennis Planning Framework Study. The CHRA identified the property at 8 Arnold Avenue as having potential heritage value for its design/physical, and historical/associative value. The Mount Dennis Secondary Plan and the associated Official Plan Amendment (OPA 571) was approved by the Ontario Land Tribunal on October 11, 2024.  
City Council listed the property at 8 Arnold Avenue on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register on May 20, 2026.
On August 19, 2026, Toronto Building received an application to demolish the dwelling at 8 Arnold Avenue. On October 14, 2026, Toronto Building issued an Applicable Law Notice to the applicant identifying outstanding requirements relating to demolition control under S.33 of the Planning Act and notice under the Ontario Heritage Act.
The owner must submit to Heritage Planning a Notice of Intention to Demolish, as required under S.27(9) of the Ontario Heritage Act, to give a municipal council at least 60 days’ notice in writing of their intention to demolish or remove a structure on a “listed” property. This allows Council time to decide whether to move forward with a notice of intention to designate the property under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act. At the time of this report, the owner had not yet submitted the notice to Heritage Planning.
Staff have determined that the property at 8 Arnold Avenue has cultural heritage value and meets three of the Ontario Regulation 9/06 criteria prescribed for municipal designation under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. A property may be designated under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act, if it meets two or more of the nine criteria.
Designation enables City Council to review proposed alterations or demolitions to the property and enforce heritage property standards and maintenance.
 Financial Impact
 There are no financial implications resulting from the recommendations included in this report in the current budget year or in future years.
The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer has reviewed this report and agrees with the information as presented in the Financial Impact Section.

 PB1.2 - 106 Beverley Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
 Consideration Type: ACTION
 Ward: 10 - Spadina - Fort York
 Origin
 (October 28, 2026) Report from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning
 Recommendations
 The Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning recommends that:
1. City Council state its intention to designate the property at 106 Beverley Street under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act in accordance with the Statement of Significance for 106 Beverley Street (Reasons for Designation) attached as Attachment 1, to the report, October 28, 2026, from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning.
2. If there are no objections to the designation, City Council authorize the City Solicitor to introduce the Bill in Council designating the property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act.
 Summary
 This report recommends that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 106 Beverley Street under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value according to the Statement of Significance which includes a description of heritage attributes found in Attachment 1.
The subject property at 106 Beverley Street, known originally as Esten House (1855), and later as Georgina House (1909), is located on the west side of Beverley Street, south of Dundas Street West, within the Grange neighbourhood of downtown Toronto.
A location map and current photograph of the heritage property are included in Attachment 2.
Constructed in 1855 for Toronto lawyer James Esten, the property contains a three-storey detached house-form building in the Italianate architectural style, which was designed by architect James Grand. Following its sale to philanthropist Georgina Broughall, who converted the property into an interdenominational women’s residence, the renamed Georgina House underwent extensive interior and exterior alterations and additions. These modifications were overseen by architect Eden Smith, including unspecified interior alterations, the front verandah (1909), a four-storey rear addition (1912), and the Osler Wing (1914), which was officially opened via public ceremony by His Royal Highness the Duke of Connaught. The property forms part of the historic residential context of the Grange neighbourhood, comprising Victorian- and Edwardian-era houses interspersed with places of worship and institutional buildings. Georgina House fits within this context of mid- to late-Victorian era houses and reflects this important period of development in Toronto.
The subject property at 106 Beverley Street was listed on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register on November 21, 1977.
This property is one of eighteen pre-1870 listed properties citywide which have been identified as candidates for designation through the City's implementation of Bill 23 amendments to the Ontario Heritage Act and its ongoing prioritization strategy for listed properties that must be designated or removed from the Heritage Register by January 1, 2027.
Part of the strategy for the review of listed properties on the Heritage Register includes the procurement of qualified heritage consultants to research, evaluate, and prepare heritage evaluation reports for a subset of listed properties prioritized for designation. City Planning retained the services of Alex Corey Heritage Consulting ("the Consultant") to research and evaluate a citywide group of eighteen pre-1870 listed properties which includes the subject property at 106 Beverley Street. The Consultant evaluated the subject property and determined that it meets the provincial criteria.
The Consultant's research on the subject property is included in Attachment 3 of this report. The research, analysis, and evaluation contained within Attachment 3 reflect the Consultant's professional expertise and opinion. Staff have independently reviewed the Consultant's research and heritage evaluation and concur with the determination that the property at 106 Beverley Street has cultural heritage value and meets five of the Ontario Regulation 9/06 criteria prescribed for municipal designation under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. A property may be designated under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act, if it meets two or more of the nine criteria.
Designation enables City Council to review proposed alterations or demolitions to the property and enforce heritage property standards and maintenance.
 Financial Impact
 There are no financial implications resulting from the recommendations included in this report in the current budget year or in future years.
The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer has reviewed this report and agrees with the information as presented in the Financial Impact Section.

City Planning retained the services of Alex Corey Heritage Consulting ("the Consultant") to research and evaluate a citywide group of eighteen pre-1870 listed properties which includes the subject property at 66 Gerrard Street East. The Consultant evaluated the subject property and determined that it meets the provincial criteria.
The Consultant's research on the subject property is included in Attachment 3 of this report. The research, analysis, and evaluation contained within Attachment 3 reflect the Consultant's professional expertise and opinion.  PB1.4 - 70 Gerrard Street East - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
 Consideration Type: ACTION
 Ward: 13 - Toronto Centre
 Origin
 (October 28, 2026) Report from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning
 Recommendations
 The Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning recommends that:
1. City Council state its intention to designate the property at 70 Gerrard Street East under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act in accordance with the Statement of Significance for 70 Gerrard Street East (Reasons for Designation) attached as Attachment 1, to the report, October 28, 2026, from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning.

A location map and current photograph of the heritage property are included in Attachment 2.
Constructed c. 1845 and substantially altered in 1886 according to plans by Langley & Burke, the property historically known as the Dr. James Elliot Graham House contains a remodelled Queen Anne Revival style, two-and-a-half-storey detached house-form building, which was originally designed in the Georgian style. Following its long tenure as a private residence, the subject property has since the 1970s been home to a series of commercial and institutional establishments and organizations, including Egerton's Restaurant, The Edge music venue, and Under 21/Covenant House. The property forms part of a group of surviving mid- to late-19-century house-form buildings around the intersection of Church Street and Gerrard Street East, in the east section of downtown Toronto.
The subject property at 70 Gerrard Street East was listed on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register on March 15, 1974.
This property is one of eighteen pre-1870 listed properties citywide which have been identified as candidates for designation through the City's implementation of Bill 23 amendments to the Ontario Heritage Act and its ongoing prioritization strategy for listed properties that must be designated or removed from the Heritage Register by January 1, 2027.

City Planning retained the services of Alex Corey Heritage Consulting ("the Consultant") to research and evaluate a citywide group of eighteen pre-1870 listed properties which includes the subject property at 70 Gerrard Street East. The Consultant evaluated the subject property and determined that it meets the provincial criteria.
The Consultant's research on the subject property is included in Attachment 3 of this report. The research, analysis, and evaluation contained within Attachment 3 reflect the Consultant's professional expertise and opinion. Staff have independently reviewed the Consultant's research and heritage evaluation and concur with the determination that the property at 70 Gerrard Street East has cultural heritage value and meets six of the Ontario Regulation 9/06 criteria prescribed for municipal designation under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. A property may be designated under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act, if it meets two or more of the nine criteria.
Designation enables City Council to review proposed alterations or demolitions to the property and enforce heritage property standards and maintenance.

 There are no financial implications resulting from the recommendations included in this report in the current budget year or in future years.

 PB1.5 - 19 Don Ridge Drive - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
 Consideration Type: ACTION
 Ward: 15 - Don Valley West
 Attention
 November 10, 2026 - A revised report from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning was posted as corrections were made to Pages 1 and 7.
 Origin
 (October 28, 2026) Report from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning
 Recommendations
 The Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning recommends that:
1. City Council state its intention to designate the property at 19 Don Ridge Drive under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act in accordance with the Statement of Significance for 19 Don Ridge Drive (Reasons for Designation) attached as Attachment 1, to the revised report, November 9, 2026 from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning.
2. If there are no objections to the designation, City Council authorize the City Solicitor to introduce the Bill in Council designating the property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act.
 Summary
 This report recommends that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 19 Don Ridge Drive under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value according to the Statement of Significance which includes a description of heritage attributes found in Attachment 1.
The subject property at 19 Don Ridge Drive, known as St. John's York Mills Anglican Church, an active Place of Worship, is located on the east side of Yonge Street, north of York Mills Road, within the York Mills neighbourhood of North York. The property also includes several structures related to the church, including the Lodge (Napier Simpson, 1958); the Dawson Lychgate, the Kay Gate, and burial grounds. The 1844 church has been the subject of additions since construction, including the Parish Hall and Auditorium (1939, 1949), and the McCollum Wing (1968). The focus of this report is the original 1844 church structure, not any of its later additions, auxiliary structures, or the adjacent burial grounds.
A location map and current photograph of the heritage property are included in Attachment 2.
The property known as St. John’s York Mills Anglican Church is a buff brick Gothic Revival church reflective of the work of the architect John George Howard and his application of a restrained Gothic style to ecclesiastical commissions through the 1840s in Upper Canada. Built as the second iteration of St. John’s York Mills Anglican Church, the present structure comprises the original 1844 church with additions from 1939, 1949, and 1968. The primary (west) façade faces southwest towards Yonge Street, and while largely obscured by mature trees today, was at one time highly visible from the valley below. While the 1844 church has been the subject of extensive additions and alterations, the integrity of John Howard’s Gothic Revival design remains intact and visible from each elevation. The additions have been designed using complementary materials, and have not subsumed the church in their scale, form, or massing, ensuring the legibility of the 1844 church from various perspectives and vantage points.
The congregation of St John’s York Mills Anglican Church traces its history back to the establishment of the Town of York in 1793, and the arrival of United Empire Loyalists to York soon after. Originally founded in 1816, the church and its original parishioners, many of whom are interred on the grounds, have deep roots within York Mills.
Today, though much of York Mills' rural character has been replaced by suburban development, there remain several area heritage properties that share a similar period of construction with St. John’s York Mills Anglican Church. These include the C.W. Jefferys House (1833; Part IV) at 4111 Yonge Street, the John Street Worker's Cottages (1860; Listed) at 4150 Yonge Street, St. John's Rectory (1878; Part IV) at 174 Old Yonge Street, the York Mills Baptist Church Manse (1850, Listed) at 106 York Mills Road, and the Jolly Miller Tavern (1857; Part IV) at 3885 Yonge Street. Collectively, and alongside the remaining natural features including the ridge and western branch of the Don River, these properties convey the history of colonial settlement and religious practice within York Mills through the nineteenth and into the twentieth centuries and are valued by the present-day community of York Mills and North York.
The subject property at 19 Don Ridge Drive was listed on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register on September 27, 2006.
This property is one of eighteen pre-1870 listed properties citywide which have been identified as candidates for designation through the City's implementation of Bill 23 amendments to the Ontario Heritage Act and its ongoing prioritization strategy for listed properties that must be designated or removed from the Heritage Register by January 1, 2027.
Part of the strategy for the review of listed properties on the Heritage Register includes the procurement of qualified heritage consultants to research, evaluate, and prepare heritage evaluation reports for a subset of listed properties prioritized for designation. City Planning retained the services of Alex Corey Heritage Consulting ("the Consultant") to research and evaluate a citywide group of eighteen pre-1870 listed properties which includes the subject property at 19 Don Ridge Drive. The Consultant evaluated the subject property and determined that it meets the provincial criteria.
The Consultant's research on the subject property is included in Attachment 3 of this report. The research, analysis, and evaluation contained within Attachment 3 reflect the Consultant's professional expertise and opinion. Staff have independently reviewed the Consultant's research and heritage evaluation and concur with the determination that the property at 19 Don Ridge Drive has cultural heritage value and meets five of the Ontario Regulation 9/06 criteria prescribed for municipal designation under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. A property may be designated under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act, if it meets two or more of the nine criteria.
In accordance with 3.1.6.50 of the Official Plan and the City's Protocol for the Identification and Review of Heritage Places of Worship, Heritage Planning staff consulted members of the Anglican Diocese of Toronto to determine if any of the heritage attributes identified in the Statement of Significance and in a future designating by-law were liturgical elements, and therefore not subject to regulation while the property remained in use by the congregation. The Anglican Diocese of Toronto confirmed that while the structure is used for liturgical purposes none of the identified attributes were liturgical elements.
Designation enables City Council to review proposed alterations or demolitions to the property and enforce heritage property standards and maintenance.
 Financial Impact
 There are no financial implications resulting from the recommendations included in this report in the current budget year or in future years.
The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer has reviewed this report and agrees with the information as presented in the Financial Impact Section.

 Toronto Preservation Board consideration on November 16, 2026
 PB1.6 - 1337 Queen Street West - Demolition and New Construction on a Designated Heritage Property under Part V, Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Approval
 Consideration Type: ACTION
 Ward: 4 - Parkdale - High Park
 Origin
 (October 28, 2026) Report from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning
 Recommendations
 The Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning recommends that:
1. City Council approve the demolition of the non-contributing building and the erection of a new 16-storey mixed-use building at 1337 Queen Street West, in the Parkdale Main Street Heritage Conservation District in accordance with subsections 42(1) 4 and 42(1) 2 of the Ontario Heritage Act, and subject to the following conditions:
a. that the replacement building for 1337 Queen Street West is constructed substantially in accordance with the plans and elevations prepared by LGA Architectural Partners dated September 25, 2026, on file with the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning.
 Summary
 This report recommends that City Council approve the demolition of an existing building on a non-contributing property located at 1337 Queen Street West within the Parkdale Main Street Heritage Conservation District (PHCD) and approve the erection of a replacement building in accordance with Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act in connection with the City-led Parkdale Hub project.
The proposed development is for the West Block of the Parkdale Hub project to erect a new 16-storey mixed-use tower with a 4-storey podium building that will include purpose-built affordable housing; and which will remain under ownership of the City.
A heritage permit for the project was previously approved on June 24 and 25, 2026, by City Council. The current proposal is largely the same as the previous approval, but a change has been made to the height of the podium of the new building. The street wall height of the new podium building has been increased by 1.2m which means that it no longer matches the height of the adjacent contributing building at 1347 Queen Street West. It also does not include the 5.0m step back required by the PHCD Plan for any parts of the new building that are taller than the adjacent contributing property. Consequently, a new Section 42 approval under the Ontario Heritage Act is required.
One of the objectives of the PHCD Plan is to conserve the consistent and continuous streetwall that characterises most of the PHCD but this section of south side of Queen Street West has neither a consistent nor a continuous street wall. Therefore, the proposed modest height increase for the podium of the new Parkdale Hub West Block development would not harm the character or appearance of the District or be contrary to the objectives of the PHCD Plan. As such staff have no concern with the lack of a step back of the top of the new podium building in this location.
 Financial Impact
 There are no financial implications resulting from the recommendations included in this report in the current budget year or in future years.
The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer has reviewed this report and agrees with the information as presented in the Financial Impact Section.
